title: Mazzoo Khan v. Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Krishna Murari, J.; Vijay Lakshmi, J.
headnote: A consumer challenging electricity bills and seeking a writ direction to decide a representation was refused relief and relegated to the alternative remedy under clause 6.5(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the writ petition was dismissed.
facts: Mazzoo Khan, a consumer of Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd., filed a writ petition in the Allahabad High Court challenging electricity bills issued to him on various grounds. He sought a direction that the authority decide his representation against those bills. Counsel for the petitioner and for the distribution company were heard on 6 May 2014.

holding_units.holding: A consumer aggrieved by electricity bills on various grounds has an alternative remedy under clause 6.5(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 before the competent authority; a writ seeking a direction to decide a representation is not liable to be granted and the petition stands dismissed, with liberty to avail that remedy.

not_decided.point: Correctness of the electricity bills and the representation
not_decided.note: The Court did not examine the grounds of challenge to the bills or the representation; the writ was dismissed solely because clause 6.5(b) afforded an alternative remedy.
